concepts.title: Random Variable
concepts.definition: A random variable is a function that associates a real number with each element in the sample space.
concepts.evidence: A random variable is a function that associates a real number with each element in the sample space.

concepts.title: Discrete Sample Space
concepts.definition: A sample space is a discrete sample space if it contains a finite number of possibilities or an unending sequence with as many elements as there are whole numbers.
concepts.evidence: If a sample space contains a finite number of possibilities or an unending sequence with as many elements as there are whole numbers, it is called a discrete sample space.

concepts.title: Continuous Sample Space
concepts.definition: A sample space is a continuous sample space if it contains an infinite number of possibilities equal to the number of points on a line segment.
concepts.evidence: If a sample space contains an infinite number of possibilities equal to the number of points on a line segment, it is called a continuous sample space.

concepts.title: Discrete Random Variable
concepts.definition: A random variable is called a discrete random variable if its set of possible outcomes is countable.
concepts.evidence: A random variable is called a discrete random variable if its set of possible outcomes is countable.

concepts.title: Continuous Random Variable
concepts.definition: A random variable is called a continuous random variable when it can take on values on a continuous scale.
concepts.evidence: When a random variable can take on values on a continuous scale, it is called a continuous random variable.

concepts.title: Probability Mass Function
concepts.definition: The set of ordered pairs $(x, f(x))$ is a probability function, probability mass function (pmf), or probability distribution of a discrete random variable $X$ if for each possible outcome $x$: (1) $f(x) \ge 0$, (2) $\sum_x f(x) = 1$, and (3) $P(X = x) = f(x)$.

concepts.title: Interval Probability for Continuous Random Variables
concepts.definition: A continuous random variable $X$ has a probability of 0 of assuming exactly any specific single value ($P(X = c) = 0$). Consequently, endpoint inclusion does not change interval probabilities: $P(a < X \le b) = P(a < X < b) + P(X = b) = P(a < X < b) = P(a \le X \le b)$.
concepts.evidence: A continuous random variable has a probability of 0 of assuming exactly any of its values.
useWhen: Evaluating probabilities over intervals with strict versus non-strict inequalities for continuous distributions
confusedWith: Cumulative Distribution Function of a Discrete Random Variable

concepts.title: Probability Density Function
concepts.definition: A function $f(x)$ is a probability density function (pdf) for a continuous random variable $X$ defined over the real numbers if: (1) $f(x) \ge 0$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$, (2) $\int_{-\infty}^\infty f(x)\,dx = 1$, and (3) $P(a < X < b) = \int_a^b f(x)\,dx$.

concepts.title: Cumulative Distribution Function of a Continuous Random Variable
concepts.definition: The cumulative distribution function $F(x)$ of a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ is defined as $F(x) = P(X \le x) = \int_{-\infty}^x f(t)\,dt$ for $-\infty < x < \infty$.

concepts.title: Relationship Between Continuous CDF and PDF
concepts.definition: For a continuous random variable with CDF $F(x)$ and density function $f(x)$, the probability over an interval is $P(a < X < b) = F(b) - F(a)$, and the density is the derivative of the CDF, $f(x) = \frac{dF(x)}{dx}$, wherever the derivative exists.
concepts.evidence: P(a < X < b) = F(b) - F(a) and f(x) = dF(x)/dx , if the derivative exists.
useWhen: Recovering the probability density function $f(x)$ by differentiating $F(x)$
Evaluating interval probabilities quickly using the CDF without direct integration
confusedWith: Cumulative Distribution Function of a Continuous Random Variable
